$\greenD{\text{Tatenda's total seconds}}-\blueD{\text{Ciara's total  seconds}}$

Tatenda spends $t$ seconds mowing each square meter, mows $700$ square meters per week, and mows for $4$ weeks.

$t(700)(4)=2800t$

We can use the expression $\greenD{2800t}$ to represent $\greenD{\text{Tatenda's total seconds}}$.

Ciara spends $c$ seconds mowing each square meter, mows $750$ square meters per week, and mows for $4$ weeks.

$c(750)(4)=3000c$

We can use the expression $\blueD{3000c}$ to represent $\blueD{\text{Ciara's total seconds}}$.

One expression to find how many more seconds Tatenda spends than Ciara spends mowing lawns during $4$ weeks is:

$\greenD{2800t}-\blueD{3000c}$

Let's see if there is another way to represent how many more seconds Tatenda spends than Ciara spends mowing lawns during $4$ weeks.

Tatenda spends $t$ seconds per square meter and mows $700$ square meters of lawn per week. So in one week, Tatenda mows for $\maroonD{700t}$ seconds.

Ciara spends $c$ seconds per square meter and mows $750$ square meters of lawn per week. So in one week, Ciara mows for $\goldE{750c}$ seconds.

That means that each week, Tatenda spends $\maroonD{700t}-\goldE{750c}$ more seconds mowing than Ciara does.

So in $\purple{4}$ weeks, he spends $\purple{4}$ times that many more seconds mowing.

We can also use the expression $\purpleD{4}(\maroonD{700t}-\goldE{750c})$ to find how many more seconds Tatenda spent in all.
We can use the expression $2800t-3000c$ or ${4}({700t}-{750c})$ to describe how many more seconds Tatenda spends than Ciara spends mowing lawns during $4$ weeks.
